summary.headline: Fairchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49.7% YoY to Rs 167 crore at a 10.5% EBITDA margin, helped by lower raw material costs after the crude soybean oil duty cut.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 167 crore (up 49.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 10.5% and net profit of Rs 10.2 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 343 crore (up 41.4%), EBITDA Rs 35.4 crore at a 10.3% margin, and net profit Rs 21.2 crore. Management attributed gains to better price realisation from lower raw material costs, higher finished product prices, and lower dimer acid imports. Plant utilisation is still low at about 60-65%, and management expects it to improve as raw material availability rises after the crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Raw material and import duty
segments.commentary: Crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%, versus earlier 27% duty on crude oils that management said made raw material too expensive. Management called the lower duty the new run rate, said some benefit is already in H1 via inventory, and said market prices are starting to soften. It declined to share the raw material mix.

segments.name: Capacity and utilisation
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 60-65% (CFO: close to 65%). Management targets 5% improvement every quarter but gave no timeline for reaching 85-90%. Management says it has not lost market share.

segments.name: New fatty-acid product
segments.commentary: Small-capacity plant using novel technology, import-substituting with export potential; commissioning has slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec quarter (after Diwali), with start-up hiccups expected. Management said the market is very large if the process succeeds, and a PFAD bypass product from palm oil is already commercialised and is a different product.

segments.name: Exports and pricing
segments.commentary: Realisation Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26. Exports to the US are on hold due to high freight costs. Value-added products (linoleic acid, distilled dimer) are expected to earn a 5-10% realisation premium. Chinese dumping has fallen, mainly due to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.

segments.name: Isostearic Acid and cosmetics
segments.commentary: Cosmetics business is expected to be hit in the near term by slowing European demand and high US import duties. Approval cycle took 2.5 years. Management expects long-term recovery since only four players globally make the product, and sees UK as the sole Cargill plant location.

segments.name: Working capital and cash use
segments.commentary: Working capital cycle guided at 90-100 days for domestic sales, longer for exports, around 100 days overall; trade receivables about Rs 100 crore. No near-term expansion plans; capex only if the new product succeeds; land of Rs 12 crore bought from promoter, already in use for operations and workers' colony.

guidance_outlook: Management is cautiously optimistic for the rest of FY27, citing Middle East crisis and global macro uncertainty.
Management expects to lift capacity utilisation as raw material availability improves; it has said it targets 5% production and volume growth every quarter.
Management did not give a quantified utilisation target; it expects 65% utilisation to rise but declined to give a number or timeline for reaching 85-90%.
Management said it would like EBITDA margins of 15-18%, but said it would maintain the current margin level rather than commit to a higher one.
Working capital cycle is expected at around 100 days, with 90-100 days for domestic sales and a longer cycle for exports.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 60-65% (about 65% per CFO), expected to improve with better raw material availability.

A small-capacity plant for a new fatty-acid product (import substitution with export potential, novel technology) is built; commissioning slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec quarter, with start-up hiccups expected.
No near-term expansion plans; management will wait for the new product before considering capex.
Company bought land worth Rs 12 crore from its promoter; the land is already used in operations and for the workers' colony.
Cost-optimisation energy-saving work is reported as complete.
demand_pricing: Realisation rose to Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 from Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26.
Q2 FY27 raw material processed 12,200 tons and sold 12,300 tons; H1 FY27 processed 24,600 tons and sold 25,800 tons. (Figures were restated inconsistently on the call for Q2 sales.)
Chinese dumping has declined, which management attributes mainly to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.
Import duty on crude soybean oil cut from 16.5% to 11%; earlier 27% duty on crude oils had raised raw material costs; management says market prices are starting to soften.
Exports to the US are on hold due to high freight costs; Isostearic Acid cosmetics demand in Europe has slowed, with cosmetic business expected to be affected near term.
Value-added products (linoleic acid for oilfield drilling, distilled dimer) are expected to carry a 5-10% realisation premium.

qa_highlights.question: What margin benefit will the import duty cut bring, and is the new run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty cut helps refiners process more soybean oil, improving raw material availability and lowering prices. It called this the new run rate, said market share was not lost, and said some benefit is already in H1 with more expected via softening prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is around 60-65%, and the CFO later put it at close to 65%. It expects 5% improvement every quarter, but gave no target for 85-90%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisations and is Chinese dumping coming back?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 versus Rs 130/kg in Q1 and Rs 106/kg a year ago. Management said it does not expect China to restart dumping, citing lower export incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new product and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fatty-acid product using novel technology, with a small plant expected to start in the Oct-Dec quarter after Diwali, with possible hiccups. It is import-substituting with export potential, and management called the market very large if the process succeeds.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach 14-15% or higher on a sustainable basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would like to see 15-18% and expects to maintain the current margin, trying to improve it further. It declined to share the raw material mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Isostearic Acid and cosmetics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European cosmetic demand is slowing and the approval cycle took 2.5 years. It expects long-term recovery because only four players make the product, and said there is no need for knee-jerk action.

risks_watch: Reversal of the crude soybean oil duty cut if oil prices fall, which could again cut raw material availability and raise costs; management sees this as unlikely given high inflation.
Possible resumption of Chinese dumping, which management believes is unlikely.
Delay or technical problems in commissioning the new fatty-acid plant, which has already slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec.
US export ramp-up depends on freight rates; European cosmetics demand is slowing.
Working capital cycle around 100 days with receivables of about Rs 100 crore; management said exports will push this higher.
Management declined to disclose raw material mix or the China import duty on edible oils.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on margins and utilisation, but evasive on quantification: management declined to give utilisation targets, raw material mix and export timelines. It is more forthcoming on the duty cut and the new product, while acknowledging delays.
